In the figure above, $\overset{\to }{OD}$ and $\overset{\to }{OE}$ are the bisectors of $∠AOC$ and $∠BOC,$ respectively. If $m∠DOC=x,$ $m∠COE=2x+{2}^{∘},$ and $m∠AOB={130}^{∘},$ find the value of $m∠BOC.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/484a70ad0c9eeca1ea03db65f5c687074189ac93f9894b64598278dc285d0d83.png)

First, let's express the measures of $∠AOC$ and $∠BOC,$ in terms of $x.$

Since $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠AOC,$ we have

$$
m∠AOC=2m∠DOC=2x.
$$

Since $\overset{\to }{OE}$ is the bisector of $∠BOC,$ we have

$$
m∠BOC=2m∠COE=4x+{4}^{∘}.
$$

Since $m∠AOB={130}^{∘},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AOC+m∠BOC & =m∠AOB \\ 2x+4x+{4}^{∘} & ={130}^{∘} \\ 6x+{4}^{∘} & ={130}^{∘} \\ 6x & ={126}^{∘} \\ x & ={21}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We are asked to find $m∠BOC.$ Substituting $x={21}^{∘}$ into the expression for $m∠BOC$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC & =4({21}^{∘})+{4}^{∘} \\  & ={84}^{∘}+{4}^{∘} \\  & ={88}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
